name: E-democracy
summary: E-democracy (digital or internet democracy) holds that information and communication technology can deepen democratic life through online information, discussion, participation and sometimes direct or delegated voting. Its adherents mostly work within existing representative systems, aiming at more active citizen involvement, transparency and responsiveness, while treating security, privacy and the digital divide as serious risks. It is a procedural outlook and takes no side on most questions of economic or social policy.
scope: The mainstream civic-tech strand: Steven Clift's definition (coined 1994, Minnesota E-Democracy), participatory and deliberative platforms such as Decidim, and liquid-democracy tools like LiquidFeedback used by Pirate Parties. It excludes e-government service delivery as such and fringe technocratic or algorithmic-rule proposals. Most economic and social statements are answered neutral with low confidence because the ideology is procedural.

sources.usedFor: Definition: ICT used by democratic actors in political and governance processes at all levels, with greater and more direct citizen participation.

universal-healthcare.rationale: E-democracy is a method of political participation, not an economic program; adherents span the spectrum on health policy.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Nothing in e-democracy's doctrine addresses wage floors; it is a procedural stance and adherents differ.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The ideology is about civic technology and participation, not market versus state allocation, so adherents are split.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Tax levels are not part of e-democracy's concerns; adherents hold varied views.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare policy is outside e-democracy's procedural focus, so there is no inferable stance.

surveillance-ok.rationale: E-democracy sources list privacy and data security as key risks, and Decidim commits never to share personal data and to hide political preferences even from administrators, which sits uneasily with broad surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Drug policy is unrelated to e-democracy; adherents are split.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Online deliberation advocates debate moderation, but the ideology takes no common line on legal speech limits.

strong-leader.rationale: E-democracy aims at more active citizen participation and revocable delegation, the opposite of a leader bypassing gridlock.

state-harmful.rationale: Its definition has governments and elected officials as legitimate democratic actors working with citizens; it seeks to improve governance, not abolish the state.

limit-guns.rationale: Gun policy has no connection to e-democracy; adherents are split.

decide-locally.rationale: Clift's definition covers local, national and international levels, but the movement began with local and municipal forums, and tools like Decidim are widely used for city participation; mildly favours local decisions.

rehabilitation.rationale: Criminal justice philosophy is outside e-democracy's scope.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Social-issue positions are not part of e-democracy; adherents vary.

more-religion-public.rationale: Religion's public role is outside e-democracy's concerns.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Substantive policy on racial justice is not an e-democracy position, though its inclusion goals touch it; neutral.

gender-social-construct.rationale: A theoretical question unrelated to civic technology; adherents split.

gradual-change.rationale: E-democracy proposals range from incremental add-ons to representative democracy to wholesale shifts toward direct models, so adherents are split.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Clift's definition mentions the international level, but nothing shows the ideology wants international bodies empowered; adherents are split.

free-trade.rationale: Trade policy is outside e-democracy's scope.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Energy policy is unrelated to e-democracy.

experts-over-public.rationale: Proponents hold that online tools let citizens inform and shape policy; Austrian parliamentarians who held that citizens were too uninformed were treated as opponents. Liquid democracy does allow delegation to experts by choice.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land taxation is a fiscal-policy question that e-democracy sources never raise; adherents differ.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Trade protection has no link to civic-technology doctrine; adherents are split.

one-party-rule.rationale: It rests on open, equal citizen participation; Decidim's contract stresses equal starting points for every proposal and universal access, incompatible with a ruling party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The ideology is defined as democratic actors using ICT in governance; hereditary rule has no place in it.

direct-votes.rationale: Clift's definition notes many see e-democracy as enabling more direct citizen involvement, and liquid democracy lets voters vote on any policy directly; yet the field also works within representative systems, so +1.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils as basis of power are not an e-democracy topic; adherents split.

natural-rulers.rationale: Decidim's social contract asserts equality of political participation and an equal starting point for every proposal, rejecting inherent fitness to rule.

military-superiority.rationale: Defence posture is unrelated to using ICT in governance.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Decidim stresses equality of participation, not of outcomes; adherents differ.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Reparations are a substantive policy outside e-democracy's concerns.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Moral egoism is not a topic in e-democracy sources; adherents vary.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Adherents favour adopting ICT in governance but sources also flag risks; no commitment to accelerating disruption.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bodily enhancement is a bioethical issue outside civic technology's scope.

algorithmic-government.rationale: E-democracy puts citizens in the decision seat via ICT; Decidim commits to traceability of how proposals are decided, and liquid democracy keeps humans delegating, so handing decisions to algorithms is not its aim.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: A Marxist-style economic aim not touched by e-democracy writers.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Decidim stresses individual privacy but collective participation; no clear stance on group rights.

exit-over-voice.rationale: E-democracy exists to expand voice, meaning participation, as the central check on government.

media-academia-power.rationale: The claim about universities and media power is not in e-democracy sources, though critics of online media exist among adherents.

total-state.rationale: Decidim's privacy and data-confidentiality commitments and its participatory design oppose a state directing all areas of life.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is not an e-democracy topic.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Macroeconomic policy is outside e-democracy's scope.

force-without-un.rationale: Use of force abroad is unrelated to e-democracy doctrine.

ban-interest.rationale: Usury law is not an e-democracy topic.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Theory of the state as class tool is not found in e-democracy sources, which treat governments as one democratic actor among several.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy production is outside e-democracy's concerns.

proportional-representation.rationale: E-democracy applies to any electoral system; adherents are split on electoral design.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Decidim's contract calls equality in political participation a fundamental principle and gives every user an equal starting point.

socialism-one-country.rationale: An internal Marxist debate that e-democracy sources do not touch.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Personal law is not an e-democracy topic.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Its aim is more active citizen participation and responsiveness in governance, rooting authority in citizens' involvement.

trade-surplus.rationale: Trade balance policy is outside e-democracy's scope.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is a deliberative-democracy idea sometimes run online, but adherents are split and sources do not endorse it.

party-controls-media.rationale: Decidim's transparency and open-content commitments, and e-democracy's reliance on open information, oppose government control of information.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The international level is within Clift's definition but there is no stance on supranational unions.

recall-officials.rationale: Revocability is a core feature of liquid democracy, and e-democracy tools are said to let voters replace poor representatives sooner.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Military alliances are unrelated to e-democracy.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: A cultural claim about rural life that e-democracy sources never make.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification is not an e-democracy topic.

death-penalty.rationale: Capital punishment is unrelated to e-democracy; adherents hold varied views.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Millian social-liberty claims are not in e-democracy sources.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: International debt policy is outside e-democracy's scope.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear strategy has no link to e-democracy doctrine.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Regulation of religious bodies is not an e-democracy topic.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Autonomy arrangements such as one country two systems are not an e-democracy topic.

character-from-environment.rationale: Nature-versus-nurture is not an e-democracy topic.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is unrelated to e-democracy.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailout policy is not an e-democracy topic.

moral-incentives.rationale: Incentive systems for labour are not an e-democracy topic.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Post-imperial influence is not an e-democracy topic.

elective-rulers.rationale: E-democracy aims at citizen participation in choosing and influencing governors; hereditary rule is opposed to its definition of democratic actors.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The ideology's purpose is increasing political participation and civic engagement; withdrawal is the opposite.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument policy is not an e-democracy topic.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Investment screening is not an e-democracy topic.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Liquid democracy has voters delegate and revoke at any time; delegates are meant to answer to those who chose them, though e-democracy as a whole is not committed to binding mandates.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Cultural critique of consumption is not an e-democracy topic.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not an e-democracy topic.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Decidim's contract commits to transparency, downloadable open data and traceability, and Clift's definition includes information sharing by governments as a core e-democracy activity.

defeat-communism.rationale: Cold-war strategy is unrelated to e-democracy.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is not an e-democracy topic.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Equal starting point for every proposal and equal participation oppose suppressing opposition.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A religious-legal doctrine unrelated to e-democracy.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Clift's definition names more active, participatory and direct citizen involvement; the Decidim contract commits to universal access and equal participation, and Wikipedia ties e-democracy to participatory and deliberative democracy.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Gender-identity law is not an e-democracy topic.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: E-democracy is not tied to a left or right camp, but adherents do not claim the division is obsolete.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The ideology grounds governance in citizens' participation, not divine authority.

social-market-economy.rationale: Economic model choice is outside e-democracy, which is procedural.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Non-alignment is not an e-democracy topic.

property-franchise.rationale: Decidim's contract gives all citizens equal participation and a unique personal digital identity; property-limited voting contradicts it, and e-democracy sources worry about unequal access.

online-participation.rationale: This is the core claim of e-democracy as defined by Clift and described in the sources.

open-government-data.rationale: Decidim's contract commits to open data, traceability and integrity of participatory records.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Procedural outlook with no stance on ecofeminist claims; adherents differ.

reification.rationale: E-democracy is about participation tools, not social theory of markets; adherents are split.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Online platforms are meant to widen who can speak, but the doctrine takes no stand on media ownership.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: E-democracy is a procedural outlook, and adherents span the spectrum on economic questions such as wealth concentration.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The ideology takes no position on military personnel policy; adherents differ.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: E-democracy takes no stance on consociational arrangements; adherents differ.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are not part of e-democracy, whose adherents differ on the question.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy, which lets people delegate votes by topic and revoke delegation at any time, is a tool used within the strand, though not all adherents adopt it.

rent-control.rationale: E-democracy is a method of participation, not an economic programme; adherents span the spectrum on rent policy.

abolish-ip.rationale: Procedural outlook with no position on intellectual property; though open-data norms exist, adherents are split on patents.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: E-democracy is a method of participation, not an economic programme; adherents split on income and ownership.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Procedural outlook; national identity and its continuity are outside e-democracy's concerns.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Procedural outlook; adherents span the spectrum on the nature of sex.

second-chamber.rationale: Adherents focus on how citizens take part, not on legislative structure, and are split.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Participatory platforms like Decidim support local participation, but the outlook does not specify confederal structures; neutral.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Privacy is valued (s3) but payments are outside the outlook; adherents are split.

online-anonymity.rationale: Decidim's social contract commits to privacy and to participation that does not require exposure, though platforms often verify residency.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Procedural outlook; it stresses equal participation, but takes no position on organising by race.

pollution-taxes.rationale: The outlook is procedural; adherents differ on environmental policy tools.

capital-controls.rationale: An economic policy question outside the procedural outlook; adherents are split.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Income policy is outside this procedural ideology; adherents hold varied economic views.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Student debt is outside this procedural ideology; adherents span the spectrum.

voter-id.rationale: Adherents split between security concerns about online voting and access concerns about the digital divide; the sources discuss security and exclusion risks.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Adherents mix a procedural view with participatory and deliberative aims such as wider citizen involvement; split.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Online participation depends on open access, and Decidim's stated principles stress transparency, privacy and equal participation, so cutoffs conflict with them.

negative-income-tax.rationale: No stand on welfare design; neutral.

race-social-construct.rationale: No stand on this question; neutral.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Platforms stress equal participation but take no position on state agencies; neutral.

homestead-ownership.rationale: E-democracy is a procedural outlook and takes no side on property theory; adherents differ.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: The ideology is about participation methods and does not address international criminal law; adherents differ.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Procedural ideology with no stance on planned economies; adherents differ.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Procedural ideology with no stance on territorial autonomy; adherents differ.

simple-living.rationale: Procedural ideology with no stance on lifestyle; adherents differ.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: E-democracy is procedural and has no stance on nationhood; adherents differ.

close-ties-china.rationale: Foreign alignment is outside e-democracy's concerns.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Resource ownership is outside e-democracy's concerns.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Social spending design is outside e-democracy's procedural focus.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The ideology is pro-technology but takes no stance on ancestral values; adherents differ.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Family law is outside e-democracy's scope.

national-resource-control.rationale: Resource control is outside e-democracy's scope.

missingStatements.text: Citizens should be able to take part in political deliberation and decisions over the internet.
missingStatements.rationale: This is the core claim of e-democracy as defined by Clift and described in the sources.

missingStatements.text: Voters should be able to delegate their vote to a representative of their choice on a given issue and withdraw that delegation at any time.
missingStatements.rationale: Delegable, revocable voting is the defining mechanism of liquid democracy, used in e-democracy tools.

missingStatements.text: Government decision-making data and citizen proposals should be published openly in downloadable formats so the public can trace how each was handled.
missingStatements.rationale: Decidim's contract commits to open data, traceability and integrity of participatory records.

missingStatements.text: Online voting in public elections should not be adopted until it can be secured against interference.
missingStatements.rationale: Wikipedia reports most experts oppose widespread internet voting because traffic cannot yet be secured, and lists security as a key risk.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow technical security question about online voting; online-participation captures the core.

notes: E-democracy is a procedural family, so most substantive policy answers are neutral and low confidence and will not count as stated positions. Strands differ: liquid democracy leans to direct and delegated voting, while others only add consultation to representative institutions.
